name: Piyusha Patil
title: MSc Computer Science @ KTH · AI / LLM Researcher · Software Engineer
tagline: I build LLM systems that are cheaper, more truthful, and actually useful. I once also helped send a rocket to 10,000 ft.
bio: I'm a Computer Science master's student at KTH Royal Institute of Technology and a Research Assistant in the ASSERT group, where I work on making LLM coding agents leaner: fewer tokens, same quality.

Before KTH I spent ~2.5 years as a Software Engineer at Protex AI (YC S21), shipping safety-intelligence products from Series A to Series B, and a year at IISc Bangalore leading ML for eVTOL aircraft simulation.
I care about LLM evaluation, hallucination detection, RAG, and agent efficiency. My hallucination-management paper won Best Paper at IEEE PuneCon 2025.

education.degree: Master of Science in Computer Science
Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Engineering

points: Researching LLM-based coding agents and inference efficiency under Prof. Martin Monperrus, contributing to SuperLean AI with the goal of reducing token consumption by 50% while preserving task performance and user experience.

Investigating tool debloating and context optimization using Jev, reducing tokens across tool definitions, descriptions, terminal commands, and agent interactions; evaluating approaches including Headroom and Ripwire.

Designing large-scale controlled experiments on SWE-bench Verified (500 real-world tasks), benchmarking agent configurations across 1,000 trials to study token efficiency, success rates, and reliability in reproducible, isolated environments.
Supporting prospective and incoming students by sharing insights into studying Computer Science at KTH and student life in Stockholm.

Representing the programme at outreach activities and events, answering questions from prospective students, and communicating the academic and student experience from a current student's perspective.
Contributing to Twiga, an open-source, LLM-powered WhatsApp assistant for Tanzanian teachers that uses RAG to deliver curriculum-grounded answers, lesson plans, and educational content.
Optimizing the retrieval pipeline by fixing document chunking and addressing oversized chunks containing up to 90% of an entire textbook that severely limited retrieval coverage and accuracy.
Working on ingestion and data-warehousing pipelines: mathematical text segmentation, chunk reprocessing, embedding regeneration, automated chunk-size validation, and citation integrity.
